old: Its name may hark back to an old word for a calm, level crossing over water.
The Maldives gave English this word for a ring of coral, by way of Portuguese sailors.
Some trace it to Sanskrit tīrtha, "ford," though a rival theory involving Persian for "water-hillock" turned out to be a dead end.
clues: This ocean landform got its English name from the people of the Maldives, whose word for it was picked up by Portuguese sailors.
It is a ring-shaped coral reef or chain of islets enclosing a calm lagoon, rather than one solid island or a straight barrier reef.
Bikini in the Pacific is a famous example, and its name may trace back to an ancient Sanskrit phrase meaning 'level ford.'
